title.narrative: IGAD 2023 - 2026 Improving Land Governance in the IGAD Region
IGAD 2023 - 2026 Improving Land Governance in the IGAD Region

description.narrative:
I ett förslag daterat april 2023 har IGAD bett Sverige att ge ekonomiskt stöd till ett projektet Improving Land Governance i IGAD-regionen med en total summa på 55 miljoner kronor under en tre-årsperiod med start i april 2023. Det nya bidraget bygger på de framgångar som har gjorts i projektet som är på väg att avslutas.
Det övergripande målet för projektet med IGAD är att förbättra gränsöverskridande markförvaltning genom kapacitetsutveckling kring innovationer inom administration, användning och förvaltning av markresurser, stärka jämställdhet mellan kvinnor och män samt ungdomars egenmakt i IGAD-regionenen.

In a proposal dated April 2023, IGAD has requested Sweden to financially support a project called Improving Land Governance in IGAD region with a total sum of SEK 55 Million over a period of three years starting in April 2023. The new contribution builds on the gains that have been made in the project that is about to end.
The overall goal of the project by IGAD is to enhance transnational land governance through capacity development on innovations in land administration, land use and management, strengthening gender equality and youth empowerment in the IGAD Region.

This second phase of this project envisions to build on the gains made over the last few years through Sida's support and has an overall goal of enhancing transnational land governance through capacity development on innovations in land administration, land use and management, strengthening gender equality and youth empowerment in the IGAD Region. The intervention has the following goals, outcome and results. Project Goal:
Enhance transnational land governance through capacity development on innovations in land administration, land use and management, strengthening gender equality and youth empowerment in the IGAD Region
Project Outcome:
The capacity of IGAD and its Member States strengthened to implement land administration reforms through the adoption and implementation of appropriate frameworks and instruments for improved service delivery, gender equality, climate change and conflict transformation.
IGADs mandate extends to policy formulation and implementation, capacity development, research and advocacy, and technological transfer. Through these approaches the following objectives will be achieved
Project Objectives
Enhance further the capacity of IGAD and its Member States to effectively implement gender responsive land administration systems through the application of innovative tools. To build climate resilience through gender responsive and conflict sensitive sustainable land use and management in the Karamoja cluster. To Improve the use and practices of youth empowerment and gender transformative approaches in land use and management. Enhance IGADs capacity to oversee the implementation of the regional land program.

title.narrative: GRANT AGREEMENT WITH IGAD IMPROVING LAND GOVERNANCCONTRIBUTION No16519

description.narrative:
Our assessment in the past two years, revealed that the contribution has encountered several challenges such as war in Sudan, loss of key personnel and competence, low level of realisation of activities and a corresponding low level of consumption of funds. This has led Sweden to consider a budget reduction of 20MSEK from the agreed 55MSEK making the total amount to go down to only 35MSEK. The budget reduction is very significant accounting about 35% of the original budget agreed. Thus, the impact of this reduction would affect the result of the project considerably. This has been analysed based on the analysis made by the partner.
Following the budget reduction the partner has revised the budget plan for the year 2025 retaining some of the original activities with some modifications, reallocation of the available budget for the introduction of new activities attainable in the existing context and retracting some others. As the overall objective of the project is a continuous process some of the project activities retracted now will be followed up in future interventions ensuring sustainability of the results.
The report(s) for the period 1st January to 31st December 2024 has been delivered on time and is complete in terms of fulfilling conditions in the Agreement. The Narrative Report provides sufficient information that enables Sida to assess the achievement of results. The reporting period observed remarkable achievement in the performance of the IGAD Land Governance Units projects implementation capacity and efficiency, played a significant role in supporting the implementation of the IGAD Land Governance Business Plan (2020- 2030).
The focus areas for the year included supporting national policy revision and/or development in Djibouti, South Sudan and Uganda; rangelands mapping and planning activities in Ethiopia, Kenya and Uganda (Somali and Karamoja Clusters); facilitating regional learning and exchange in Ethiopia and Uganda; building capacity on gender responsive climate change adaptation in Djibouti, Kenya and Uganda and addressing barriers to securing equal land rights for women. Through these initiatives, the implementation of activities moved from purely regional work to in-country as well as the cross-border areas mainly in the Somali and Karamoja Clusters.
The financial report is presented according to the requirements in the article on financial reporting in the agreement (including appendices). The financial report provides information about the amount of funds that has been forwarded to Implementing Partners which have received funds during the year.
MAJOR IMPACTS, LESSONS LEARNT AND CHALLENGES
Coordination among government institutions, Civil Society Organizations, academia, development partners has been improved and hence encouraging positive responses registered from stakeholders on land policy paradigm. This is a foundation for mobilizing all land actors across sectors and at all levels to drive the land reform processes in the Member States while developing and implementing National Land Policies.
Bringing together diverse stakeholders from government agencies, producer organizations, research institutions, development agencies, civil society organizations and the private sector enables collaboration across sectors. Stakeholders must engage in constructive dialogues and work collectively to address the multifaceted challenges facing the Member States and the cluster at large.
Continuous sensitization and awareness creation on the land use planning objectives, processes and outputs amongst key actors and interest groups should be undertaken to ensure integration of various policies and inform the public on land use issues and best practices.
Recognition and calls to build and strengthen local cross border structure/framework for managing shared resources. The improving land governance in Somali Cluster has strengthened interactions and engagement between the local government officials in charge of administration as well as technical departments such as land, livestock, water, agriculture and rangelands. The security agencies have also been involved because the project teams and participants keep on crossing the borders. As a result of these increased engagements and collaborations, there are calls for establishment and formalization of local cross border structure bringing together all the key cross border agencies/stakeholders/departments to deal holistically with the cross border shared resource management in a conflict sensitive and gender responsive way. Currently there is a tri-border forum dealing with the promotion of cross border trade.
Some of the challenges experienced during this reporting period include frequent staff turnover, Inadequate resources to prepare Mandera County Spatial Plan and community led initiatives
As 2025 will be the final year of the contribution the activity plan has been prepared taking in to account the agreement amendment made in 2025. Accordingly, the plan and budget for the upcoming period assessed to be eligible and in line with the latest agreement amendment made in 2025. It is also noted that reasonable adjustments and realignment to the programme has been considered based on previous experience and the situation in specific implementing countries in the region.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
